strings.name: Michelle Obama
strings.role: Lawyer · author · public advocate · former US first lady
strings.summary: Raised on Chicago’s South Side, Obama graduated from Princeton and Harvard Law School, working in law, community service and university public affairs. US first lady from 2009 to 2017, she championed children’s health, military families and girls’ education. After the White House she continued through foundation work, speeches, screen projects and books including Becoming. Her 2025 book The Look explores public image and personal expression.

strings.timeline.t1.title: Published The Look
strings.timeline.t1.text: With Meredith Koop and other collaborators, explored clothing, public image and personal expression.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Published The Light We Carry
strings.timeline.t2.text: Drew on personal experience to discuss connection, resilience and self-understanding in uncertain times.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Published Becoming
strings.timeline.t3.text: Recounted her Chicago childhood, legal and public-service career and White House life.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Advanced Let Girls Learn
strings.timeline.t4.text: Worked with the Obama administration to support adolescent girls’ education globally.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Co-launched Joining Forces
strings.timeline.t5.text: Joined Jill Biden in an initiative supporting service members, veterans and their families.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Launched Let’s Move!
strings.timeline.t6.text: Advanced children’s health through nutrition, physical activity and school food environments.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Became US first lady
strings.timeline.t7.text: Became the first African American first lady at Barack Obama’s inauguration, serving until 2017.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed legal studies
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned her Harvard law degree and joined Sidley Austin in Chicago.
